title: Detlev Bronk named as an MJ12 member

tellings.quote: In fact, Detlev Bronc who is the president of the Rockefeller Foundation was named as one of the Majestic 12.

plain: Detlev Bronk, whom Michels calls president of the Rockefeller Foundation, is named in the MJ-12 papers as one of the "Majestic 12", a supposed secret group of twelve set up to deal with crashed flying saucers. Michels brings this up himself, and if it were so, it would put a leading figure of American science inside a hidden UFO effort. The papers came to light on a roll of film mailed anonymously in 1984 to a man named Jaime Shandera and were made public in 1987. The National Archives and the Truman and Eisenhower libraries found no trace of them, and FBI copies are marked "BOGUS", but researchers still disagree about whether they are genuine. The briefing paper lists "Dr. Detlev Bronk" among the members and says that "a similar analysis of the four dead occupants was arranged by Dr. Bronk" and that his team coined the term "Extra-terrestrial Biological Entities". Bronk's part holds only as far as the paper is genuine.

discussion.text: A typed briefing paper dated 18 November 1952, with a Truman memorandum to Secretary Forrestal of 24 September 1947 as its Attachment A, that came to light on a roll of 35mm film Jaime Shandera received anonymously at his Burbank home in 1984 and that he, William Moore and Stanton Friedman then studied; it was made public in 1987. The National Archives and the Truman and Eisenhower Libraries report their searches for it negative. The FBI's Majestic 12 file holds copies sent to it in 1988 and 1991, each marked "BOGUS" by hand, and records that the Air Force Office of Special Investigations "advised on November 30, 1988, that the document was fabricated" and that "the document is completely bogus". Philip Klass called the Truman memo an obvious fraud; Friedman judged the briefing paper and the memo "almost certainly genuine". The briefing paper lists "Dr. Detlev Bronk" among the twelve members and gives him more than a name: "A similar analysis of the four dead occupants was arranged by Dr. Bronk", and "Dr. Bronk's team has suggested the term "Extra-terrestrial Biological Entities", or "EBEs"". Michels reports the naming as the paper makes it; Bronk's membership and his team's work hold only as far as the paper is genuine.
